channel.title: UK Defence Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from UK Defence Journal (ukdefencejournal.org.uk)

item.title: UK deploys Typhoon jets to Qatar in Middle East
item.description: The deployment involves 12 Squadron, the joint UK–Qatar Typhoon unit, and is being carried out at the invitation of the Qatari government. The post UK deploys Typhoon jets to Qatar in Middle East first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: British vessels shadow Russian warship off coast
item.description: Royal Navy ships and aircraft were activated to monitor Russian naval movements in the English Channel during a two-day operation conducted in coordination with NATO allies. The post British vessels shadow Russian warship off coast first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Britain to test launch new ballistic missiles next year
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has set out new details on its Nightfall deep-strike missile programme for Ukraine, confirming development contracts will be awarded this spring, with production expected to begin in late 2027. The post Britain to test launch new ballistic missiles next year first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: JFD and ST Engineering expand naval cooperation in Singapore
item.description: JFD Global has signed a new agreement with ST Engineering Marine aimed at widening their long-running cooperation in Singapore and extending collaboration into international markets. The post JFD and ST Engineering expand naval cooperation in Singapore first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Report urges reforms to unlock SME role in UK defence
item.description: A new report by Babcock and the University of Exeter shows that small and medium sized enterprises could play a significantly larger role in strengthening UK defence resilience, but warns that structural barriers continue to limit their participation. The post Report urges reforms to unlock SME role in UK defence first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: UK approvals required for US use of bases
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that decisions on whether the United States can use its military bases in the UK for operational purposes are taken on a case-by-case basis and require UK approval. The post UK approvals required for US use of bases first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: MV Isle of Islay sails on homecoming voyage to Scotland
item.description: The MV Isle of Islay has begun her maiden voyage from the Cemre shipyard in Turkey, setting sail for Scotland following her official handover. The post MV Isle of Islay sails on homecoming voyage to Scotland first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Dalzell steel shortage judged low risk to FSS ship build
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has said the current shortage of raw materials at Liberty Steel’s Dalzell plant is assessed as posing a low risk to the construction of the Royal Navy’s future Fleet Solid Support ships. The post Dalzell steel shortage judged low risk to FSS ship build first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Eight Polish helicopter pilots to train in UK from 2026
item.description: Eight Polish military helicopter pilots will begin training in the UK from the 2026 to 2027 training year, the Ministry of Defence has confirmed in a written parliamentary answer. The post Eight Polish helicopter pilots to train in UK from 2026 first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Babcock chief to step down after driving huge turnaround
item.description: Babcock International has confirmed that chief executive David Lockwood will retire by the end of the year, bringing to a close a five-year turnaround that has reshaped the defence engineering group and driven a sharp recovery in its financial performance. The post Babcock chief to step down after driving huge turnaround first appeared on UK Defence Journal.
